messages:
nina: vendor asks for a one-time SIEM export of auth+request logs for tenant=ember-corp to satisfy their compliance audit. They want full 12 months of logs and an S3 copy. Is that even a supported flow? cc @sara @kevin

sara: Short answer: we don't do broad raw exports without strict gating. Two options: 1) saved search + scrubbed snapshot, 2) controlled export via export-proxy with JIT unwrap and evidence TTL. Which does the vendor need?

sam: If the vendor only needs aggregated facts, prefer saved search and a CSV/JSON snapshot with PII redacted. Full S3 export is heavy - legal will push back.

kevin: Technical constraints: our export-proxy can stream to customer-forensics bucket and apply transform hooks. Default retention on forensics-store is 30d. KMS envelope wrapping is applied; unwrap requires a ticketed KMS-proxy call.

nina: They specifically requested 12 months (regulatory) and want the data in their cloud. Tradeoff: send scrubbed/aggregated or allow timeboxed vendor access to our export artifact?

sara: Vendor outbound transfer needs additional controls: signed, time-limited artifact + data-sharing MOU. Prefer handing them a scrubbed artifact and not granting direct bucket access. For >30d retention or outbound transfer, require sec + legal + vendor risk signoff.

infra-bot: Export-proxy request checklist: `ticket_id`, `requester`, `vendor_name`, `data_scope`, `time_window`, `fields_to_redact`, `retention_ttl`, `destination`, `evidence_chain`. Include sample saved search and scrubbed preview.

legal-bot: Data sharing note: any export that leaves Redwood domain triggers vendor data review. Need: data minimization statement, data transfer agreement, and POA for >90d retention. Also check cross-border implications for tenant region.

kevin: Practically: run saved search, produce scrubbed artifact, attach to ticket for legal to review. If vendor still needs raw logs, sec-lead must approve and we create an ephemeral export role that only writes a single object and then revokes. We do not maintain long-term vendor access keys.

sam: Example saved search we can offer to the vendor (no PII):
``` 
index=auth tenant=ember-corp earliest=-12mon latest=now
| stats count by date_bin(1d), action, status
| where action IN ("login","token_refresh","logout")
```
This returns counts rather than raw session tokens.

sara: If vendor claims regulatory need for full records, require vendor to supply legal basis + DPA amendment. After that: sec-lead + infra-svc + legal approve, infra runs export-proxy with KMS unwrap audit and writes artifact to inbound vendor bucket with enforced TTL via lifecycle.

nina: What about KMS rotation? If we rotate CMKs, will the vendor be unable to decrypt older artifacts? We need assurance artifacts remain decryptable for the retention window.

kevin: We use envelope encryption with a stable archive-wrapping key and key rotation policy that supports decryption of older objects via key ACLs. Rewrapping can be scheduled as part of archival pipeline. Document the CMK id and include it in the evidence_chain so forensics can prove continuity.

infra-bot: Reminder: any KMS unwrap operation will emit kms:Decrypt to audit-bucket with `ticket_ref` metadata. Maintain `evidence_chain` in ticket for chain-of-custody automation.

legal-bot: Also note: outbound transfer to vendor requires an entry in the vendor data register and an assigned data steward. Include those fields in the ticket.

nina: Vendor insisted on their own S3. If we must push to their bucket, will infra accept a signed PUT (we push) instead of giving them access?

kevin: Yes. We can push the artifact to vendor-provided signed URL or SFTP endpoint. But we still require: scrubbed artifact, TTL set at upload, ACL blocking public read, and both sec + legal signoff.

sara: RBAC aside: product/dev teams cannot request these exports directly. Must route via sec sponsor. For vendor onboarding changes (external principal IAM), that lives with identity and compliance. No ad-hoc role grants.

sam: If approved, we create ephemeral role `vendor_export_<ticket>` that runs the export job and auto-deletes. Access logs will show which principal triggered export.

nina: Requested TTL they want: 365d. Legal already said POA for >90d. Do we have a path to get to 365d for a compliance audit?

legal-bot: 365d retention for exported data is possible but requires: updated DPA clause, sec-lead signoff, vendor security assessment, and CIRO (or CISO office) approval. Timeline: expect 3-5 business days after documentation.

kevin: Operational note: if retention >90d, we must ensure archival key management and long-term decrypt test, include a monthly integrity hash and snapshot to a locked evidence vault. Add that to ticket as requirement.

infra-bot: Action checklist appended to ticket when created. Fields to include: `retention_deviation_reason`, `dpa_attachment`, `vendor_security_assessment`, `evidence_hash_schedule`.

nina: OK I'll open ticket SEC-EXPORT-178741 for the vendor export. I'll attach saved-search preview and request initial 30d scrubbed artifact while we work legal for longer TTL.

sara: Good plan. Tag sec-lead and legal in the ticket. We'll triage and keep this thread updated. :white_check_mark:
